I can’t give exact revenue numbers from that chart as described. Without any numeric axis labels or the source data, any “exact” figures would be fabricated. I can, however, help in three reliable ways — pick one:

1) I can extract near-exact values if you attach the chart image (or paste a screenshot). With the image I’ll digitize the bars and give numbers plus an uncertainty estimate.

2) I can walk you step‑by‑step so you can extract exact values yourself (fast). Two good options:
   - Use WebPlotDigitizer (recommended):
     1. Go to https://automeris.io/WebPlotDigitizer/.
     2. Upload the chart image.
     3. Choose “Bar plot” or “2D (X-Y) plot”.
     4. Calibrate the y-axis: if there are no numeric labels you’ll need to enter the numeric value that the top (or any) gridline represents — if you don’t know that, ask the chart author for the axis max.
     5. Click each bar to record its height and export as CSV.
   - Manual pixel method (if you prefer not to use a web tool):
     1. Open the image in an editor that shows pixel coordinates (e.g., Paint, Preview, Photoshop).
     2. Note the y pixel of the chart baseline (y0) and the top gridline or chart top (yMaxPixel).
     3. For each bar, note the top y pixel (yi). Compute relative height = (y0 - yi) / (y0 - yMaxPixel).
     4. Multiply relative height by the known y-axis maximum value to get the numeric revenue. (Again: you must know the numeric value that corresponds to the chart top or a gridline.)

3) If you want quick approximate estimates without an image, I can produce rough guesses (with clear uncertainty ranges) based on a verbal description of how each bar lines up with the gridlines — but these will not be “exact” and I’ll flag them clearly.

Which would you like? If you choose option 1, please attach the image. If option 2, say which method and I’ll guide you. If option 3, describe how each month’s bar aligns with the gridlines (e.g., “Jan is just below the 50k gridline; Feb is about halfway between 50k and 100k,” etc.) and I’ll estimate with ranges.
